author: coordinator
intent: Recover the original CPU classification and flag-probe behavior using an explicitly observed intrinsic-capable compiler for a minimal owner TU
evidence: Pinned original 0x0063E860-0x0063E94E toggles AC bit0x40000, clears output bytes9C0830/9C0B70 before the first gate, restores saved flags only after AC success, sets rank1, then toggles ID bit0x200000 without a final restoration. CPUID0 compares EBX/EDX/ECX vendor words, signed-compares maximum leaf against1, and CPUID1 maps base families5/6 and MMX bit0x800000 to ranks2..5; unsupported families clear rank. Preserve all these quirks.

Mapped caller 0x00639330 immediately overwrites AL with byte9C0830 after calling the probe; source ignores the return. Original saves/restores EAX, not an int0 result. Void interpretation is supported at that known caller only; full indirect/executable caller coverage and entry-register/condition-flag fidelity remain obligations. Do not claim ABI equivalence or full original matching.

Actual clang-cl i686 generated PUSHFD/POPFD/CPUID without source assembly through the existing configured compiler protocol. VC6 LINK6 accepts the no-debug COFF control, but rejects the Z7 CodeView control with LNK1103. A narrowly selected intrinsic frontend must explicitly omit incompatible debug metadata, record its real executable/preprocessing closure/effective argv, preserve ordinary VC6 routing, and export its actual application recipe. No silent fallback or full-Caviar modern compilation.

Current rank storage is private in Caviar's anonymous namespace, vendor storage is external, and neither has a source object binding. Establish correct source-owned byte starts and coordinated declarations/ownership before splitting the probe; do not infer complete original allocation extents. Source owns mappings; caches remain ignored.

Ship compiler interaction as project-local code behind existing entrypoints, not library-specific VC6 or Caviar adapters or a new CLI. Require fail-closed compiler-selection/reproducibility/receipt controls, pinned original branch evidence and actual-source hardware-mock tests, scoped historical continuity, independent review, relevant native measurements and fresh full application build/link. Preserve matching obligations; compiler controls are not game acceptance.

Actual VC6 debug-link controls reject even Clang's minimal compiler-identification CodeView section. Its companion llvm-objcopy --strip-debug removes that metadata and permits the control to debug-link. Generic compile-file evidence must explicitly distinguish primary compiler output from ordered postprocessed final output; retain strict v1 parsing, observe actual stage argv/tools/inputs and hash continuity, and refuse stage-ignorant build-graph comparison. Trusted capture and final object/link byte correspondence do not prove transformation semantics or acceptance. This narrow package scope expansion is driven by the real CPU recovery blocker, not authorization for unrelated framework work.

Independent review also requires a closed compiler-argument policy, disabled default Clang config, implicit environment/target/language/debug override controls and a nonempty external-global relocation fixture. Register the optional frontend explicitly in project-owned configuration rather than silently requiring its binaries in every ordinary-only project toolchain. Keep the original task baseline and all discoveries.

Fresh pinned instruction review confirms both gates branch on full flags-word XOR equality, not only the toggled bit. The first toggle/read precedes rank/vendor zeroing, which precedes JE at63E886. CPUID0 receives saved flags in ECX and CPUID1 receives CPUID0 vendor-word ECX; retain these inputs through __cpuidex and preserve unproved final condition-flag effects as an obligation.

The existing toolchain SDK-path test assumes an ordinary-only registry and now fails under the explicitly enabled mixed-toolchain policy. Extend this test file only to distinguish disabled ordinary-only discovery from enabled registered toolchain merging, with no implicit tool lookup in disabled mode. Enabled mixed projects deliberately require their declared compiler tools; this is not a fallback or evidence of matching.
